it irks me verb

also I’m loath to, I can’t be bothered, I hate to, be reluctant, it vexes me, if you don’t mind, regret

classical

Plaut. Ps. 281: Nimiō id quod pudet facilius fertur quam illud quod piget.
Ter. Ad. 3.3.37: frātris mē quidem piget pudetque (Lewis & Short)

piget, pigēre, piguit (pigitum est)

impersonal verb: accusative of the person, with the genitive of the thing or an infinitive (mē piget)

it irks, it vexes; one is loath to, one is sorry for

Donatus on that line: pudet quod turpe est; piget quod dolet. Nisi piget, if you don’t mind.

Examples

  • Nimiō id quod pudet facilius fertur quam illud quod piget. Nōn dedisse istunc pudet: mē quia nōn accēpī piget.

    What shames a man is far easier to bear than what vexes him. He is ashamed of not having paid; I am vexed at not having been paid.Plaut. Ps. 281–282

  • Adulēscēns, quaesō hercle ēloquere tuom mihi nōmen, nisi piget.

    Young man, do please tell me your name, if you don’t mind.Plaut. Men. 1066

See also I’m ashamed, I’m sorry, mind.

SourcesLewis & Short: pigeo

Plautus, Menaechmi 1066; Pseudolus 281–282.
